top.description: Big-name prospects flipping during the early signing period has become less common over the years, but the days leading up to it tell a different story. Coaches aren't only focused on closing out the regular season; they're also making last-minute pitches to players or scheduling last-minute visits to make one final impression. The top players in the country are already committed to their respective programs, but that doesn't mean that they're locked in until they've signed on the dotted line. Who are some of the biggest names to watch heading into the early signing period? Now at Buford (GA), while he hasn't locked down his commitment to Texas Tech, that hasn't stopped other programs from taking their shots at him. He remained steadfast in his commitment to Texas Tech even after visits to Florida, LSU, Texas and SMU. The rumor mill once again began to swirl when Brewster showed up in Baton Rouge for LSU's game against Texas on Nov. 14. top.title: Ryan Clark says Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished because it was ‘never built on character’
top.description: Credit: The Pivot, ESPN The final act of Aaron Rodgers’ career took a pretty shocking turn this week. The future Hall of Famer was unceremoniously benched via a social media post late Tuesday night with little explanation. In response, he showed up on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and threw his longtime coach Mike McCarthy under the bus, accusing him of falling asleep in meetings and several other shortcomings in his first year in Pittsburgh. We’ve seen great players leave the league far from their peak. Tom Brady got his last Super Bowl with the Buccaneers, but his final season in Tampa Bay was far from pretty. But nothing in that final season affected Brady’s status amongst the all-time greats. Given Rodgers’ exit was so loud, and according to many former pros , so against the unwritten rules of football life , will Rodgers see his reputation take a hit due to how this chapter ends? Ryan Clark doesn’t think so. Speaking on his show The Pivot , Clark, who has been public with his feelings about Rodgers for some time, argued that the quarterback’s legacy as a player was safe, because it was never tied to him being a good guy. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy is in no way tarnished, because his legacy was never built on character,” Clark said. “If Tom Brady says this when leaving the New England Patriots, we’re shocked. We’re surprised. Because it’s against everything he’s ever shown us. Mike McCarthy should’ve known that kissing a rattlesnake was safer than coaching Aaron Rodgers again. He’s shown many times there’s no loyalty, there’s nothing I won’t say, I won’t think about the person I’m talking about before I think about myself. Many people will say that he fell on the sword. That this was about the team. Well, you’re already out of the building. This is about you.” Clark noted that the fact that Rodgers’ former teammates were forced to answer so many questions about his departure was proof that his actions weren’t about helping the team. “Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that to be some sort of martyr. Aaron Rodgers did that because he got demoted and said, ‘Oh, I’m going to get you way more than you could get me.'” From there, Clark lamented what has become of his former team , arguing that he was against the hiring of McCarthy in the first place as it went against what the Steelers usually looked for in a coach. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished, because it was never built on character” Multiple things can be true at once. Aaron Rodgers can be both right & wrong. Telling the truth doesn’t preclude you from being disingenuous, & Mike McCarthy can have a winning record while operating like a bad head coach. top.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 25: Cairo Santos #2 of the Chicago Bears lines up a field goal attempt in the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 25, 2021 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this week’s edition of the Gridiron Time Machine, we’re revisiting an unlikely comeback at Arrowhead, a valuable lesson in why you should never kick to Devin Hester, and a Thanksgiving victory that came down to the final second. So hop aboard the time machine for another fantastic trip down memory lane. 1.) 1993, Bears @ Chiefs: An unlikely comeback at Arrowhead November 21, 1993 | Bears win 19-17 The Bears entered Week 12 of the 1993 season with a 4-5 record under first-year head coach Dave Wannstedt. A trip to Arrowhead Stadium to face the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs wasn’t exactly the ideal opportunity to get back to .500. Things certainly didn’t look promising early on, as future Hall of Fame running back Marcus Allen found the end zone twice to give Kansas City a 14-0 lead in the second quarter. The Bears managed to get on the board before halftime thanks to a pair of Kevin Butler field goals from 32 and 45 yards out, cutting the deficit to eight. Chicago continued chipping away in the third quarter when Tim Worley broke loose for a 25-yard touchdown run. A blocked extra point kept the Bears from pulling within one, and a Nick Lowery field goal extended Kansas City’s lead to 17-12 heading into the fourth quarter. If you were expecting Jim Harbaugh to lead some sort of aerial assault to complete the comeback, think again. Harbaugh completed 13 of his 20 pass attempts for just 98 yards and two interceptions, finishing the afternoon with a passer rating of 37.1. He was considerably more effective with his legs, rushing for 56 yards on eight attempts. The Bears leaned heavily on their ground game, rushing for 185 yards on 43 attempts. Worley led the way with 59 yards, while Neal Anderson added another 42. With just over three minutes remaining, Anderson punched it in from one yard out to give Chicago its first lead of the afternoon. The Bears’ defense, which recorded five sacks and held Kansas City to just three second-half points, made sure that lead stuck. The Chiefs would go on to win the AFC West and reach the AFC Championship Game that season, but on this particular Sunday, the Bears had their number. Winning on the road against one of the AFC’s best teams without throwing for 100 yards? top.title: 3 Keys to Victory: Michigan Football at Ohio State
top.description: In the blink of an eye, Michigan’s season went from a complete and utter failure to what could be a similar story to the 2024 season. The Wolverines were 6-5 going into The Game in 2024, but the outlook on the season completely changed when it upset the No. 1 team in the country.Michigan’s 6-5 team of 2026 doesn’t have that exact same opportunity, but after beating then-No. 4 UCLA last week, it would feel similar if it capped the season off with a win over the Buckeyes. It’s the biggest game of the year, no matter the records or circumstances, as Michigan and Ohio State meet for the 122nd rendition of The Game. Here are the keys to victory for the Wolverines. Win the turnover margin Last week proved exactly why the turnover margin is so important in football, and how damaging it can be for a Michigan team that has struggled with that aspect of the game all season long. UCLA entered last Saturday with a +16 turnover margin, the best in the Big Ten and tied for second in the FBS. The Wolverines forced three turnovers and only turned it over once — the final takeaway leading to a game-altering touchdown at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Michigan is still last in the Big Ten with a -8 turnover margin, but Ohio State isn’t great either with a -3 turnover margin, tied for 14th in the conference. If it needs reminding, three of the Wolverines’ biggest wins — Week 2 against Oklahoma, Week 7 against Penn State, Week 11 against UCLA — have been the only games they won the turnover margin. One of the only faults of this Michigan defense has been its inability to force turnovers, but if last week was an indication of how The Game will go, it could be a long day for an Ohio State offense that has turned the ball over seven times in the last four games, three of which ended in losses. Keep a strong run game Freshman running back Savion Hiter had himself a game against the Bruins. For an offense that’s been struggling to find its footing all season long, especially in the run game, his performance proved something replicable. Hiter had a career-high 26 carries for 104 yards against UCLA, and it was his second consecutive game with more than 100 yards rushing. Ohio State has the 15th -best rushing defense in FBS, allowing just 100.3 yards per game. Even with the injuries and blunders of the Buckeyes’ offense, the defense has remained intact and hasn’t allowed more than 116 yards rushing to an opponent in the last four weeks, despite three of them ending in losses. If the Michigan offense can limit the negative run plays caused by blocking issues along the line, and rally behind Hiter and the run game to spark the offense, it may score just enough points to win. Continue making field goals The unsung heroes of Michigan’s win over UCLA was freshman kicker Jacob Baggett and punter Cam Brown, the latter of whom handled some difficult snaps as the holder. top.description: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 15: Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up on the sideline during the NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Atlanta Falcons on November 15, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix exits the Week 11 bye and enters a seven-game stretch that could define his career. With scrutiny mounting , the final two months of 2026 will not only dictate whether Penix remains the Falcons’ starter entering 2027, but could also determine whether he ever gets another shot to lead an NFL franchise. To save his job, Penix must show immediate growth in three critical areas: starting faster, surviving pocket pressure, and rediscovering his signature deep ball. Penix must fix his first-quarter freeze According to Next Gen Stats , the Falcons’ slow starts have been fueled by a 31st-ranked first-quarter EPA per play and 32nd-ranked first-quarter passing yards. Leaning on the run game would help, with Atlanta’s early-game run rate plummeting from 56 percent in Penix’s first three starts to the 24th-ranked 42 percent over the last five. But the Falcons cannot ask star running back Bijan Robinson to carry the entire offense, as Penix has to pull some weight. Per NFL.com , Penix has completed 46 percent of his throws in the first quarter while averaging just 3 yards per attempt. The Falcons have produced just six passing first downs in the first quarter in Penix’s eight starts, compared with an NFL average of 19. This keeps the team from sustaining offense, thanks to a league-low first-quarter third-down efficiency of 10 percent across Penix’s starts. This isn’t a problem unique to 2026, as Penix posted a dismal 38.8 passer rating in the first quarter during his rookie season before surging to 108.8 in his second. That leap offers hope that more time in Tommy Rees’ offense can spark a similar turnaround. But as a third-year pro, Penix’s early-game struggles are harder to excuse, and Atlanta cannot afford to wait until 2027 for competence. Pressure is Penix’s kryptonite While the slow starts are problematic, they at least show growth potential. However, Penix’s biggest issue is his inability to handle pressure. top.title: Rain, wind gusts up to 30 mph expected for 49ers-Seahawks showdown
top.description: Rain falls during the fourth quarter of an NFC Divisional Playoffs game between the Green Bay Packers and the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., on Jan. 20, 2024. (Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Sunday's pivotal matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks is set to be played in wet and windy weather . In a phone interview with SFGATE on Friday, National Weather Service meteorologist Dial Hoang said rain is expected to hit the Bay Area on Sunday morning. The rain will likely roll in from the North Bay, where it's expected to arrive shortly after sunrise, and reach Santa Clara County and the area surrounding Levi's Stadium in the late morning. Once it arrives, it won't go away for the rest of the day, he said. "We're looking at the rain continuing across the Bay Area during the game, and especially after the game," Hoang told SFGATE. "Those lingering showers may extend into Monday morning." It shouldn't be overly cold - the forecast calls for temperatures to be in the mid-60s - and shouldn't rain too heavily, with around a quarter of an inch expected. But Hoang said it will be "gusty" during Sunday's game, with wind gusts expected to be between 25 and 30 mph. "It does look like the wind is going to be a strong factor," Hoang said. It's been a wet few weeks in the Bay Area, with a Nov. 18 storm breaking rainfall records in various Bay Area cities and causing flooding in several pockets of San Francisco. The region also saw near-historic high tides last week as part of the ongoing impact of El Niño this winter. The 49ers have already made several preparations in anticipation of a rainy winter. While the players and coaches were training in Colorado Springs, Colorado, to prepare for a game in Mexico City last week, the 49ers built a rain canopy over one of their practice fields in Santa Clara. Why does this now exist at #49ers HQ? Kyle Shanahan: "Because I keep getting told about El Niño or something" https://t.co/dh4iWI49Mk - Harrison Rich (@harrisonrich_) November 25, 2026 When asked during a news conference why the team opted to add the canopy, head coach Kyle Shanahan quipped, "Because I keep getting told about El Niño or something," before explaining its benefits, which can give the 49ers the closest thing to the bubble-like indoor facilities that many football teams have across the country. top.title: UH's 'Old Man Club' prepares for final home game after 15 combined college football seasons
top.description: Brandon Mack II's eight-year college odyssey comes to an end with UH on Saturday. (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) They've heard all the jokes about their age, how long they've played college football and all the changes they've witnessed. Meet defensive linemen Brandon Mack II and Quindario Lee, card-carrying members of the University of Houston' s unofficial "Old Man Club." When the No. 18 Cougars host Baylor for Senior Night on Saturday, two of the longest-tenured players in school history will play their final home game. Eight seasons for Mack. Seven seasons for Lee. UH vs. BAYLOR: How to watch "A lot of stories with those guys, a lot of memories," said James Ross III, the Cougars' edges and defensive run-game coordinator. Both are 25 years old. Mack goes by the nickname "Unc." Lee, who is three months older, is called "Gramps." "B-Mac always reminds me I'm older," Lee said with a laugh. And you'll likely never see their type of longevity again. The NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, which limits players to five seasons within a five-year window, will make it impossible to replicate careers that have combined for 15 seasons and spanned two presidential terms. "I'm just excited to see them transition into life," Ross said. He jokingly added, "We tried to find some more years. There are no more hidden years anywhere else." Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . While there is no official category, Mack and Lee are believed to be the longest-tenured players in program history. Their careers have been prolonged by an extra year of eligibility because of the COVID-19 pandemic and medical redshirts. A three-star defensive end out of high school, Mack signed with Ole Miss in 2018. He spent four seasons in Oxford, missing one with a foot injury, before transferring to UH in 2023. His first season with the Cougars ended prematurely, however, when he suffered a high-grade tear of the lat muscle on his left side in the second week of the season. He has been healthy the past three seasons, playing in 12 games in 2024 and set to play 13 games in consecutive seasons with the Cougars qualifying for a bowl. "I feel like yesterday was my first time in TDECU Stadium when we played UTSA and wore our powder blue jerseys," said Mack, who has posted 10 sacks over the past three seasons. "Then you blink and it's over. It definitely felt like it went by fast." Mack thought his college career was over last November. He began filling out information for the Cougars' Senior Night ceremony when he was told he had another year of eligibility. Lee's path has been just as winding. A three-year defensive lineman, Lee went from small-town Alabama to Fort Scott (Kan.) Community College. He transferred to Central Michigan, where he played 24 games over three seasons, before arriving at UH in 2024.

top.title: Space in Macy’s 100 Thanksgiving Day parades
top.description: null The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is sure to be a blast, but it is a bit light on "space." According to previews provided by the department store chain, the founder of the New York City holiday celebration, space fans turning up or tuning in to catch sight of an astronaut or other nod to NASA will have only a returning rocket to look forward to on Saturday (Nov. 28). (The parade has been postponed two days from Thursday, Nov. 26, due to bad weather.) Not that Macy's (or the space agency) has hinted about anything cosmic planned for the 100th parade; it's only that the event has had a long history of celebrating space exploration with its floats and balloons. "For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . Weighty weightless man The earliest space-themed feature of the parade may have been the "Space Ship," a float that made its first appearance in the 19th procession in 1945 and in various configurations — with and without astronauts and planets — appeared on and off through 1962. Perhaps more memorable, though, and certainly much larger, was the "Spaceman" (or, more appropriately, "The Giant Spaceman"). The 70-foot-long (21-meter) helium balloon made its debut in 1952, nine years before the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. Described by Macy's as an "artist's conception of a visitor from another planet," the humanoid figure had a black spacesuit , a silver helmet and boots, a jet propulsion backpack and a black rocket gun. Once the heaviest balloon in the parade, the "Spaceman" was created by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company years before anyone had entered space. (Image credit: Macy's) Ironically, for a figure garbed for the weightless environment of space, the Spaceman was for a long time the parade's heaviest giant balloon. At 600 pounds (272 kilograms), it was only tied by the Pink Panther in 1988 and then exceeded two years later by Bart Simpson. The rubber Spaceman was created by Goodyear Tire, the same company that contributed hardware to NASA's Apollo program , including the wire mesh non-pneumatic tires for the lunar roving vehicle. The Spaceman survived being torn when it was caught with a lamppost in 1955, and a helium shortage resulting in it and other balloons being filled with air and held up by cranes in 1958. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic had a rough Friday night in San Antonio. The Los Angeles Lakers lost 99-96 to the San Antonio Spurs , dropping their season record to 15-4. The loss also knocked Los Angeles out of the NBA Cup. Things got even worse for Doncic after the final buzzer. As he walked toward the tunnel at the Frost Bank Center, he got into an argument with a fan sitting near the walkway. Video from the arena showed Doncic tossing his wristband to a female fan. A moment later, he heard she did not want it. top.title: “I’m Just like Shaq Free-Throw Shooting-Wise” – Victor Wembanyama Humbly Admits to Struggling at the Line As Lakers Legend Catches Stray
top.description: Shaquille O'Neal, Victor Wembanyama © X/ @Lakers, @spurs San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama admitted he was struggling at the free-throw line and compared himself to Los Angeles Lakers legend Shaquille O’Neal. Wembanyama missed five of his eight attempts at the line in Friday’s 99-96 win over the Lakers, including a crucial one up-three with 57 seconds left. Stephon Castle saved Wembanyama by knocking down a 3 and giving the Spurs a six-point lead. Wembanyama missed another free throw up two with just over two seconds left, but made his final attempt that sealed the Spurs’ win. Dissecting his underwhelming display at the charity stripe, Wembanyama told Prime Video analysts he was like O’Neal at the free-throw line. “I gotta say, I’m just like Shaq free-throw shooting-wise right now,” he said. O’Neal was one of the worst free-throw shooters in the league, and teams often fouled him in the clutch because of it. O’Neal was often benched when opponents played the foul game while trailing in close games. The Lakers legend shot 52.7% from the free-throw line. Wembanyama is much better over his career. Entering Friday’s game, he was a career 81.3% free-throw shooter and 77.8% on the season. Although it’s a career-low mark, Wembanyama is still one of the better shooting bigs in the NBA from the free-throw line. Victor Wembanyama’s elite rebounding allows Spurs to complete comeback win over Lakers Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs trailed by 20 points in the first half. However, they crawled back in the second half, inspired by Wembanyama’s elite two-way display. After managing only eight points and five rebounds in the first half, Wembanyama bounced back with 17 points and 11 rebounds in the second. His rebounding was decisive in that stretch. The Lakers won the 50-50 battles in the first half, but once Wembanyama locked in, there wasn’t much Los Angeles could do to stop the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Wembanyama finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, four steals and two blocks, overcoming an inefficient shooting night with hustle and effort in other areas. Wembanyama may have also got the edge in the MVP race against rival Luka Doncic. nigeria.title: Why Tinubu should stay in office for 10 years – Akande
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Osun State Governor, Bisi Akande, has called for President Bola Tinubu to remain in office for 10 years, saying the period would allow him to complete ongoing projects and deliver lasting reforms. Akande made the call during an interview on the Frankly Speaking with Icon podcast, published on Friday. “He should remain in office, if possible, for another 10 years; otherwise, we go back to the situation of ‘Ebinpawa’ because there has been a foundation for hunger,” Akande said. He cited the Olubadan’s comments on road projects across the South-West, including routes linking Ijebu-Ode, Abeokuta, Oyo and Ikire, as evidence of the administration’s ongoing work. Quoting the traditional ruler, Akande said: “If you are working like this, and this had not been done 50 years before you, what again do we still say you should do, and you have not done? “But so that you will be able to complete this good job that you started, Ibadan people and Oyo State people are supporting you to do another four years.” Akande also blamed successive military administrations for what he described as decades of neglect of agriculture, education and economic development, saying their policies contributed to the country’s present difficulties. “Forty years before he came, since 1966, when the military started ruling you, you have been laying the foundation for hunger. You have abandoned your farms. You have abandoned the job. You have refused to be educated. You have refused to be modernised,” he said. He expressed optimism that Tinubu’s policies would produce significant improvements in the coming years, particularly in electricity supply and modernisation. “So in another 10 years there will be electricity everywhere. There will be modernisation,” he said. “They liberalised electricity. If you have money today, you can create electricity in your home. You can create it in your city. You can create it around you,” he said. Comparing the policy with the restrictions under previous military administrations, Akande said individuals were previously prevented from generating electricity independently. “Unlike what the military did before, if you tried to create electricity, they would arrest you. They would make you a debtor. They wouldn’t let you do it. They said only the Federal Government could do it. Tinubu came and said everybody can do it,” he added. On his own public engagements, the former governor attributed his reduced movement around the country to age, contrasting his present situation with when he was younger. nigeria.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
nigeria.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. It was renamed Yusuf Maitama Sule University in 2017 before reverting to its original name in 2024 following an amendment to the state law establishing it. nigeria.title: UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash
nigeria.description: UEFA has opened disciplinary investigations into violent incidents involving supporters of Marseille and Besiktas during their respective Europa League fixtures on Thursday. The European football governing body announced the probes on Friday, following clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters in France and a confrontation between Besiktas fans and police in Georgia. In Marseille, several hundred home supporters confronted visiting Levski Sofia fans, leaving five Bulgarian supporters hospitalised. French magistrates have also launched an investigation into alleged intentional violence involving some Marseille supporters. Authorities are equally examining allegations of incitement to hatred following claims of Nazi salutes and provocations by Bulgarian fans. Meanwhile, Besiktas’ encounter with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was temporarily halted after clashes broke out between supporters and police. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. The relocation came amid worsening diplomatic relations between Turkey and Israel following the outbreak of the Gaza war. nigeria.title: Why I turned down Burna Boy’s 85/15 demand – Aristokrat boss, Peedi Picasso
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku Peedi Picasso, CEO of Aristokrat Records, has opened up on why he refused to renew Burna Boy’s record deal, saying the singer demanded an 85-15 per cent revenue split in his favour. Picasso, whose real name is Piriye Isokrari said their previous deal gave Burna Boy 60 per cent, while the label took 40 per cent. He also revealed that the singer’s mother insisted he should only sign two-year contracts, a condition that influenced the label’s decision. According to Picasso, the proposed increase did not make financial sense at the time because the label was not making significant money from record sales. Picasso said live performances and endorsement deals were the major sources of revenue. He argued that accepting an 80-20 or 85-15 split would have left the label with a smaller share of the income despite the money it was investing in the singer. Picasso said the arrangement was difficult to justify for another two-year contract, particularly because the label was not entering a long-term deal. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Held under the theme “Celebrating Partnerships, Rewarding Excellence,” the event brought together company leadership and long-standing partners from Northern, Eastern and Western Nigeria. entertainment.title: Inside the 2026 WISCAR Mentoring Walk
entertainment.description: Mentors, mentees, professionals and members of the public gathered at Eko Atlantic, Lagos, on Saturday, November 14, 2026, for the annual Women in Successful Careers (WISCAR) Mentoring Walk . Led by WISCAR Founder and Chairperson, Amina Oyagbola , the walk forms part of the lead-up to the organisation’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference. Participants were paired up for the walk along the Eko Atlantic, each with someone they had not met before. At the end of the route, they switched to new mentor-mentee partners for a short mentoring session, which gave everyone two fresh conversations in one morning. Back at the meeting point, participants shared what they had learnt from their partners, from career advice to personal lessons. Nutritionist Sherese Ijewere then led a session on healthy eating and answered questions on everyday food choices. Coach Bobbie Tee of Happy Heart Fitness, closed the morning with a Zumba session. Next stop: the conference The walk sets the stage for WISCAR’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference , themed “ Courage in Action: Shaping Policies and Structures for Inclusive Progress. ” The conference takes place on Saturday, November 28, 2026, at the Civic Centre, Lagos. Highlights include: A keynote from Dr Ndidi Nwuneli , former President and CEO of the ONE Campaign and Founder of LEAP Africa, who will also receive this year’s Distinguished WISCAR Award. Speakers including Badejo-Okusanya , SAN, President of the Nigerian Bar Association, and Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, President of the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management (CIPM) The launch of WISCAR’s CIPM-endorsed Corporate Mentoring Playbook The graduation of Cohort 2 of the Women in Law Mentoring Programme Register now at https://wiscar.ng/almc . sports.title: Ryan Clark says Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished because it was ‘never built on character’
sports.description: Credit: The Pivot, ESPN The final act of Aaron Rodgers’ career took a pretty shocking turn this week. The future Hall of Famer was unceremoniously benched via a social media post late Tuesday night with little explanation. In response, he showed up on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and threw his longtime coach Mike McCarthy under the bus, accusing him of falling asleep in meetings and several other shortcomings in his first year in Pittsburgh. We’ve seen great players leave the league far from their peak. Tom Brady got his last Super Bowl with the Buccaneers, but his final season in Tampa Bay was far from pretty. But nothing in that final season affected Brady’s status amongst the all-time greats. Given Rodgers’ exit was so loud, and according to many former pros , so against the unwritten rules of football life , will Rodgers see his reputation take a hit due to how this chapter ends? Ryan Clark doesn’t think so. Speaking on his show The Pivot , Clark, who has been public with his feelings about Rodgers for some time, argued that the quarterback’s legacy as a player was safe, because it was never tied to him being a good guy. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy is in no way tarnished, because his legacy was never built on character,” Clark said. “If Tom Brady says this when leaving the New England Patriots, we’re shocked. We’re surprised. Because it’s against everything he’s ever shown us. Mike McCarthy should’ve known that kissing a rattlesnake was safer than coaching Aaron Rodgers again. He’s shown many times there’s no loyalty, there’s nothing I won’t say, I won’t think about the person I’m talking about before I think about myself. Many people will say that he fell on the sword. That this was about the team. Well, you’re already out of the building. This is about you.” Clark noted that the fact that Rodgers’ former teammates were forced to answer so many questions about his departure was proof that his actions weren’t about helping the team. “Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that to be some sort of martyr. Aaron Rodgers did that because he got demoted and said, ‘Oh, I’m going to get you way more than you could get me.'” From there, Clark lamented what has become of his former team , arguing that he was against the hiring of McCarthy in the first place as it went against what the Steelers usually looked for in a coach. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished, because it was never built on character” Multiple things can be true at once. Aaron Rodgers can be both right & wrong. Telling the truth doesn’t preclude you from being disingenuous, & Mike McCarthy can have a winning record while operating like a bad head coach. sports.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 25: Cairo Santos #2 of the Chicago Bears lines up a field goal attempt in the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 25, 2021 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this week’s edition of the Gridiron Time Machine, we’re revisiting an unlikely comeback at Arrowhead, a valuable lesson in why you should never kick to Devin Hester, and a Thanksgiving victory that came down to the final second. So hop aboard the time machine for another fantastic trip down memory lane. 1.) 1993, Bears @ Chiefs: An unlikely comeback at Arrowhead November 21, 1993 | Bears win 19-17 The Bears entered Week 12 of the 1993 season with a 4-5 record under first-year head coach Dave Wannstedt. A trip to Arrowhead Stadium to face the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs wasn’t exactly the ideal opportunity to get back to .500. Things certainly didn’t look promising early on, as future Hall of Fame running back Marcus Allen found the end zone twice to give Kansas City a 14-0 lead in the second quarter. The Bears managed to get on the board before halftime thanks to a pair of Kevin Butler field goals from 32 and 45 yards out, cutting the deficit to eight. Chicago continued chipping away in the third quarter when Tim Worley broke loose for a 25-yard touchdown run. A blocked extra point kept the Bears from pulling within one, and a Nick Lowery field goal extended Kansas City’s lead to 17-12 heading into the fourth quarter. If you were expecting Jim Harbaugh to lead some sort of aerial assault to complete the comeback, think again. Harbaugh completed 13 of his 20 pass attempts for just 98 yards and two interceptions, finishing the afternoon with a passer rating of 37.1. He was considerably more effective with his legs, rushing for 56 yards on eight attempts. The Bears leaned heavily on their ground game, rushing for 185 yards on 43 attempts. Worley led the way with 59 yards, while Neal Anderson added another 42. With just over three minutes remaining, Anderson punched it in from one yard out to give Chicago its first lead of the afternoon. The Bears’ defense, which recorded five sacks and held Kansas City to just three second-half points, made sure that lead stuck. The Chiefs would go on to win the AFC West and reach the AFC Championship Game that season, but on this particular Sunday, the Bears had their number. Winning on the road against one of the AFC’s best teams without throwing for 100 yards? There are always drills that involve catching the ball, both standing still and on the move. There is also a JUGS machine guys can use at the end of practice. Several players use it all the time. sports.title: 3 Keys to Victory: Michigan Football at Ohio State
sports.description: In the blink of an eye, Michigan’s season went from a complete and utter failure to what could be a similar story to the 2024 season. The Wolverines were 6-5 going into The Game in 2024, but the outlook on the season completely changed when it upset the No. 1 team in the country.Michigan’s 6-5 team of 2026 doesn’t have that exact same opportunity, but after beating then-No. 4 UCLA last week, it would feel similar if it capped the season off with a win over the Buckeyes. It’s the biggest game of the year, no matter the records or circumstances, as Michigan and Ohio State meet for the 122nd rendition of The Game. Here are the keys to victory for the Wolverines. Win the turnover margin Last week proved exactly why the turnover margin is so important in football, and how damaging it can be for a Michigan team that has struggled with that aspect of the game all season long. UCLA entered last Saturday with a +16 turnover margin, the best in the Big Ten and tied for second in the FBS. The Wolverines forced three turnovers and only turned it over once — the final takeaway leading to a game-altering touchdown at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Michigan is still last in the Big Ten with a -8 turnover margin, but Ohio State isn’t great either with a -3 turnover margin, tied for 14th in the conference. If it needs reminding, three of the Wolverines’ biggest wins — Week 2 against Oklahoma, Week 7 against Penn State, Week 11 against UCLA — have been the only games they won the turnover margin. One of the only faults of this Michigan defense has been its inability to force turnovers, but if last week was an indication of how The Game will go, it could be a long day for an Ohio State offense that has turned the ball over seven times in the last four games, three of which ended in losses. Keep a strong run game Freshman running back Savion Hiter had himself a game against the Bruins. For an offense that’s been struggling to find its footing all season long, especially in the run game, his performance proved something replicable. Hiter had a career-high 26 carries for 104 yards against UCLA, and it was his second consecutive game with more than 100 yards rushing. Ohio State has the 15th -best rushing defense in FBS, allowing just 100.3 yards per game. Even with the injuries and blunders of the Buckeyes’ offense, the defense has remained intact and hasn’t allowed more than 116 yards rushing to an opponent in the last four weeks, despite three of them ending in losses. If the Michigan offense can limit the negative run plays caused by blocking issues along the line, and rally behind Hiter and the run game to spark the offense, it may score just enough points to win. sports.title: Final Audition: 3 fixes Michael Penix needs to save his Falcons future
sports.description: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 15: Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up on the sideline during the NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Atlanta Falcons on November 15, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix exits the Week 11 bye and enters a seven-game stretch that could define his career. With scrutiny mounting , the final two months of 2026 will not only dictate whether Penix remains the Falcons’ starter entering 2027, but could also determine whether he ever gets another shot to lead an NFL franchise. To save his job, Penix must show immediate growth in three critical areas: starting faster, surviving pocket pressure, and rediscovering his signature deep ball. Penix must fix his first-quarter freeze According to Next Gen Stats , the Falcons’ slow starts have been fueled by a 31st-ranked first-quarter EPA per play and 32nd-ranked first-quarter passing yards. Leaning on the run game would help, with Atlanta’s early-game run rate plummeting from 56 percent in Penix’s first three starts to the 24th-ranked 42 percent over the last five. But the Falcons cannot ask star running back Bijan Robinson to carry the entire offense, as Penix has to pull some weight. Per NFL.com , Penix has completed 46 percent of his throws in the first quarter while averaging just 3 yards per attempt. The Falcons have produced just six passing first downs in the first quarter in Penix’s eight starts, compared with an NFL average of 19. This keeps the team from sustaining offense, thanks to a league-low first-quarter third-down efficiency of 10 percent across Penix’s starts. This isn’t a problem unique to 2026, as Penix posted a dismal 38.8 passer rating in the first quarter during his rookie season before surging to 108.8 in his second. sports.title: Rain, wind gusts up to 30 mph expected for 49ers-Seahawks showdown
sports.description: Rain falls during the fourth quarter of an NFC Divisional Playoffs game between the Green Bay Packers and the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., on Jan. 20, 2024. (Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Sunday's pivotal matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks is set to be played in wet and windy weather . In a phone interview with SFGATE on Friday, National Weather Service meteorologist Dial Hoang said rain is expected to hit the Bay Area on Sunday morning. The rain will likely roll in from the North Bay, where it's expected to arrive shortly after sunrise, and reach Santa Clara County and the area surrounding Levi's Stadium in the late morning. Once it arrives, it won't go away for the rest of the day, he said. "We're looking at the rain continuing across the Bay Area during the game, and especially after the game," Hoang told SFGATE. "Those lingering showers may extend into Monday morning." It shouldn't be overly cold - the forecast calls for temperatures to be in the mid-60s - and shouldn't rain too heavily, with around a quarter of an inch expected. But Hoang said it will be "gusty" during Sunday's game, with wind gusts expected to be between 25 and 30 mph. "It does look like the wind is going to be a strong factor," Hoang said. It's been a wet few weeks in the Bay Area, with a Nov. 18 storm breaking rainfall records in various Bay Area cities and causing flooding in several pockets of San Francisco. The region also saw near-historic high tides last week as part of the ongoing impact of El Niño this winter. The 49ers have already made several preparations in anticipation of a rainy winter. While the players and coaches were training in Colorado Springs, Colorado, to prepare for a game in Mexico City last week, the 49ers built a rain canopy over one of their practice fields in Santa Clara. Why does this now exist at #49ers HQ? Kyle Shanahan: "Because I keep getting told about El Niño or something" https://t.co/dh4iWI49Mk - Harrison Rich (@harrisonrich_) November 25, 2026 When asked during a news conference why the team opted to add the canopy, head coach Kyle Shanahan quipped, "Because I keep getting told about El Niño or something," before explaining its benefits, which can give the 49ers the closest thing to the bubble-like indoor facilities that many football teams have across the country. "Sometimes, when it's just like a monsoon out there and we're playing in a bubble, you can get a little bit more done with not being in that [rain]," Shanahan said. "So, if it ends up being like that, like people have warned, it's nice that at least we can walk through and stuff like that." It was sunny at the Niners' practice on Friday in Santa Clara, but the team is practicing with the rain in mind. With starting quarterback Brock Purdy out with an ankle injury, backup Mac Jones was spotted squirting water onto the football to help practice throwing a "wet ball," similar to what the team is expecting on Sunday.

sports.title: UH's 'Old Man Club' prepares for final home game after 15 combined college football seasons
sports.description: Brandon Mack II's eight-year college odyssey comes to an end with UH on Saturday. (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) They've heard all the jokes about their age, how long they've played college football and all the changes they've witnessed. Meet defensive linemen Brandon Mack II and Quindario Lee, card-carrying members of the University of Houston' s unofficial "Old Man Club." When the No. 18 Cougars host Baylor for Senior Night on Saturday, two of the longest-tenured players in school history will play their final home game. Eight seasons for Mack. Seven seasons for Lee. UH vs. BAYLOR: How to watch "A lot of stories with those guys, a lot of memories," said James Ross III, the Cougars' edges and defensive run-game coordinator. Both are 25 years old. Mack goes by the nickname "Unc." Lee, who is three months older, is called "Gramps." "B-Mac always reminds me I'm older," Lee said with a laugh. And you'll likely never see their type of longevity again. The NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, which limits players to five seasons within a five-year window, will make it impossible to replicate careers that have combined for 15 seasons and spanned two presidential terms. "I'm just excited to see them transition into life," Ross said. He jokingly added, "We tried to find some more years. There are no more hidden years anywhere else." Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . While there is no official category, Mack and Lee are believed to be the longest-tenured players in program history. Their careers have been prolonged by an extra year of eligibility because of the COVID-19 pandemic and medical redshirts. A three-star defensive end out of high school, Mack signed with Ole Miss in 2018. He spent four seasons in Oxford, missing one with a foot injury, before transferring to UH in 2023. His first season with the Cougars ended prematurely, however, when he suffered a high-grade tear of the lat muscle on his left side in the second week of the season. He has been healthy the past three seasons, playing in 12 games in 2024 and set to play 13 games in consecutive seasons with the Cougars qualifying for a bowl. "I feel like yesterday was my first time in TDECU Stadium when we played UTSA and wore our powder blue jerseys," said Mack, who has posted 10 sacks over the past three seasons. "Then you blink and it's over. It definitely felt like it went by fast." Mack thought his college career was over last November. He began filling out information for the Cougars' Senior Night ceremony when he was told he had another year of eligibility. Lee's path has been just as winding. A three-year defensive lineman, Lee went from small-town Alabama to Fort Scott (Kan.) Community College. He transferred to Central Michigan, where he played 24 games over three seasons, before arriving at UH in 2024.

sports.title: Detroit Lions’ playoff, NFC North odds still high despite loss to Bears

(Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ loss to the Chicago Bears was deflating and disappointing. Not so much because it was a critical game for Detroit’s playoff odds, but because the Lions were in a prime position to win and take a stranglehold on the division. But as you’ll soon see, the Lions are still in a great position to accomplish everything in front of them. Let’s look at how their playoff, NFC North, and even Super Bowl odds have shifted after their Thanksgiving loss to the Bears. Postseason odds: NYT simulator: 78% (down 8%) RBSDM: 81% (down 4%) DVOA: 83.3% (down 6.3%) ESPN (FPI): 91.5% (down 5.5%) Even by the most pessimistic models, the Lions still have more than a 3-in-4 chance to make the postseason. Their loss to the Bears did not decrease their postseason odds by more than 10% across any of these four prediction models. ESPN still remains very high on the Lions, with a massive 91.5% chance to make the playoffs, but it seems like the more normal average is around 80-83%. NFC North title odds NYT simulator: 15% (down 14%) RBSDM: 20% (down 13%) DVOA: 19.3% (down 18%) ESPN (FPI): 30.6% (down 19.4%) Obviously, this loss had a bigger impact on Detroit’s chances to win the division, but the odds are not outstandingly long still. The Lions still have a 15-30% chance to win the NFC North, and that stands true because they still have three division games left. And while they’re all on the road, Detroit has proven they can go toe-to-toe with any of those teams. And the fact that Detroit has a 2-1 record in the division already gives them a nice leg up on the tiebreakers, as long as they continue to beat their divisional foes. NFC’s No. 1 seed NYT simulator: 4% (down 4%) RBSDM: 6% (down 6%) DVOA: 3.9% (down 6.3%) ESPN : 5% (down 6%) You can pretty much kiss the Lions’ odds for the No. 1 seed goodbye. Unless the San Francisco 49ers struggle down the stretch—and they do have tough games against the Seahawks, Giants, Rams, and Chiefs left—Detroit is not likely to finish any higher than the NFC’s No. 2 seed. Super Bowl appearance odds ESPN (FPI): 11.0% (down 1.9%) DVOA: 7.3% (down 3.1%) Surprisingly, the Lions’ Super Bowl odds have not been impacted too much. Perhaps their strong offensive performance against a decent Bears defense has fed the models’ optimism about Detroit being able to survive a shootout game. However, their defensive performance on Thursday looms large as well.

science.description: null The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is sure to be a blast, but it is a bit light on "space." According to previews provided by the department store chain, the founder of the New York City holiday celebration, space fans turning up or tuning in to catch sight of an astronaut or other nod to NASA will have only a returning rocket to look forward to on Saturday (Nov. 28). (The parade has been postponed two days from Thursday, Nov. 26, due to bad weather.) Not that Macy's (or the space agency) has hinted about anything cosmic planned for the 100th parade; it's only that the event has had a long history of celebrating space exploration with its floats and balloons. "For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . Weighty weightless man The earliest space-themed feature of the parade may have been the "Space Ship," a float that made its first appearance in the 19th procession in 1945 and in various configurations — with and without astronauts and planets — appeared on and off through 1962. Perhaps more memorable, though, and certainly much larger, was the "Spaceman" (or, more appropriately, "The Giant Spaceman"). The 70-foot-long (21-meter) helium balloon made its debut in 1952, nine years before the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. Described by Macy's as an "artist's conception of a visitor from another planet," the humanoid figure had a black spacesuit , a silver helmet and boots, a jet propulsion backpack and a black rocket gun. Once the heaviest balloon in the parade, the "Spaceman" was created by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company years before anyone had entered space. (Image credit: Macy's) Ironically, for a figure garbed for the weightless environment of space, the Spaceman was for a long time the parade's heaviest giant balloon. The rubber Spaceman was created by Goodyear Tire, the same company that contributed hardware to NASA's Apollo program , including the wire mesh non-pneumatic tires for the lunar roving vehicle. science.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
science.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. science.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

science.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
science.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? science.title: Astronomers watch a red giant star greedily devour a stellar 'Bao bun' before erupting: 'We couldn't quite believe our luck'
science.description: null Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER). "The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events." Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy , a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion. Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years, They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. They linked this to a star called WNTR23bzdiq / WTP19aalzlk that had been observed steadily brightening since 2019 after being stable for the preceding 30 years. Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. The team theorizes that Big Bao, with a mass seven times greater than the sun, expanded so rapidly and violently that it swallowed its smaller companion star. The unfortunate star, Little Bao, then spiraled into Big Bao's core in fewer than 10 orbits. "A couple of years back, we discovered a star that was gradually brightening. science.description: A detail from Joseph Wright’s 1771 painting The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus, showing Henning Brand in 1669 Science History Images/Alamy Imagine you could boil the development of science down to a single ingredient. A magical, mystical compound that transformed human history. Of course, science doesn’t work that way; even if breakthroughs shift the paradigm of our understanding, discovery doesn’t progress like a tech tree in a computer game, but as an interweaving tapestry of complementary and competing ideas and experimentation. Theories can bubble under the surface for centuries, overlooked because of politics or failure to realise their implications, while innovations can emerge from taking an idea in one industry and transplanting it to another. But, for a moment, try and picture what just one such ingredient could be. What would you pick? For centuries, in medieval Europe, alchemists quested for the “Philosopher’s Stone” that would finally help them achieve their dreams of transmutation. It was a search doomed to failure from the very beginning. And yet, a far better idea was under their noses – or, rather, their underpants – the entire time. My pick? Urine has a strong case for being the most transformative substance in human history. It required the first chemical reaction we mastered – fire – to keep us warm, cook our food and smelt ores. But leatherwork played an equally key role. Urine is a source of urea, which bacteria can break down into ammonia, granting early humans easy access to a base that could soften organic matter and tan hides. Across the world, leatherwork became the cornerstone of survival for every civilisation, from the Americas to Europe, Africa and Asia: even cultures that didn’t develop a bronze age, such as the Aztec, or skipped it entirely, as seen in Sub-Saharan Africa, relied on leatherwork for clothes, structures, industry and commerce. In ancient Rome, urine was so useful for laundries to keep togas whiter-than-white that Emperor Vespasian levied a tax on draining urinals. When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on November 8, 2026, clouds encroached on the snowy mountain on Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula . But they hovered beneath the volcano’s 3,283-meter (10,771-foot) peak, leaving a clear opening over its caldera and northern upper slopes. The upper reaches of Shivelyuch feature a caldera 9 kilometers (5.6 miles) wide that is open to the south. A lava dome , formed by vents extruding viscous magma, appears as a dark area within it. Lava domes on Shivelyuch go through cycles of growth and collapse, with collapses sometimes setting off fast-moving avalanches of hot ash and rock called pyroclastic flows . In November 2026, effusive eruptions of lava and explosive activity at Shivelyuch had been ongoing for months , according to reports from the Kamchatka Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT). And despite frequent cloudiness, satellites regularly detect thermal anomalies from the volcano. On the day of this image, KVERT reported that a plume of resuspended ash drifted 120 kilometers (75 miles) to the east. That kind of activity is relatively tame for the mountain. Explosions from Shivelyuch periodically send ash several kilometers up into the atmosphere, where it can travel great distances and pose risks to aircraft . In July 2026, an ash plume rode the jet stream over the Bering Sea into Alaskan airspace, according to news reports , prompting the cancellation of multiple flights. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor.

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories.
